03b. Dialogues on Democracy: Method Checks (Attrition, Speeders, Conversation Detail, Power)

Shaye

2026-10-27

Checks behind the Method section and Appendix A: demographics, differential attrition by condition, differential exclusion of speeders, the evidence-count measure, and post hoc power and sensitivity for the pairwise condition comparisons. The sample and attrition tables the supplement reads are produced by 03a_method_descriptives.R.

Set Up

Demographics

Differential Attrition

df_all$messageType <- factor(df_all$messageType)
df_all$ConditionFeedback <- factor(df_all$ConditionFeedback)
df_all$ConditionChat <- factor(df_all$ConditionChat)


da.all.s1 <- df_all %>% filter(ScreenedDummy == 0, Study == 1)
da.all.s2 <- df_all %>% filter(ScreenedDummy == 0,Study == 2)

da.s1$messageType = relevel(da.s1$messageType,ref="Qualtrics  + Adversarial Dialogue")
da.s2$ConditionFeedback = relevel(da.s2$ConditionFeedback,ref="Control")

##overall DA----
    #chi square version

report(chisq.test(da.s1$AttritDurExp,da.s1$messageType)) #full condition attrition 
## Effect sizes were labelled following Funder's (2019) recommendations.
## 
## The Pearson's Chi-squared test of independence between da.s1$AttritDurExp and
## da.s1$messageType suggests that the effect is statistically significant, and
## small (chi2 = 25.72, p < .001; Adjusted Cramer's v = 0.13, 95% CI [0.05, 1.00])
report(chisq.test(da.s1$AttritDurExp,da.s1$ConditionChat))
## Effect sizes were labelled following Funder's (2019) recommendations.
## 
## The Pearson's Chi-squared test with Yates' continuity correction of
## independence between da.s1$AttritDurExp and da.s1$ConditionChat suggests that
## the effect is statistically significant, and very small (chi2 = 13.26, p <
## .001; Adjusted Cramer's v = 0.10, 95% CI [0.05, 1.00])
report(chisq.test(da.s1$AttritDurExp,da.s1$ConditionFeedback))
## Effect sizes were labelled following Funder's (2019) recommendations.
## 
## The Pearson's Chi-squared test of independence between da.s1$AttritDurExp and
## da.s1$ConditionFeedback suggests that the effect is statistically significant,
## and very small (chi2 = 8.36, p = 0.015; Adjusted Cramer's v = 0.07, 95% CI
## [0.00, 1.00])
report(chisq.test(da.s2$AttritDurExp,da.s2$ConditionFeedback))
## Effect sizes were labelled following Funder's (2019) recommendations.
## 
## The Pearson's Chi-squared test of independence between da.s2$AttritDurExp and
## da.s2$ConditionFeedback suggests that the effect is statistically not
## significant, and tiny (chi2 = 0.59, p = 0.744; Adjusted Cramer's v = 0.00, 95%
## CI [0.00, 1.00])
fig.da <- ggbarstats(
  data = da.s1,
  y = Condition,
  x = AttritDurExp)+
  scale_fill_economist()
## Scale for fill is already present.
## Adding another scale for fill, which will replace the existing scale.
fig.da

extract_stats(fig.da)

# Differential Attrition by Condition (Logistic Regression)
res_da_s1 <- clean_regress(
  da.s1,
  dvs = "AttritDurExp",
  type = "logistic",
  predictors = ~ messageType,
  dv_labels = c(AttritDurExp = "Study 1 Attrition")
)

##DA by covariate----
# Interaction models between condition and participant characteristics
res_da_int_list <- list(
  Race = clean_regress(da.s1, dvs = "AttritDurExp", type = "logistic", predictors = ~ messageType * Race, dv_labels = c(AttritDurExp = "Attrition x Race")),
  Age = clean_regress(da.s1, dvs = "AttritDurExp", type = "logistic", predictors = ~ messageType * Age, dv_labels = c(AttritDurExp = "Attrition x Age")),
  Gender = clean_regress(da.s1, dvs = "AttritDurExp", type = "logistic", predictors = ~ messageType * GenderClean, dv_labels = c(AttritDurExp = "Attrition x Gender")),
  Education = clean_regress(da.s1, dvs = "AttritDurExp", type = "logistic", predictors = ~ messageType * Education, dv_labels = c(AttritDurExp = "Attrition x Education")),
  DemRep = clean_regress(da.s1, dvs = "AttritDurExp", type = "logistic", predictors = ~ messageType * DemRep_C.text, dv_labels = c(AttritDurExp = "Attrition x Party")),
  Religion = clean_regress(da.s1, dvs = "AttritDurExp", type = "logistic", predictors = ~ messageType * religion, dv_labels = c(AttritDurExp = "Attrition x Religion")),
  VoteMethod = clean_regress(da.s1, dvs = "AttritDurExp", type = "logistic", predictors = ~ messageType * VoteMethod.text, dv_labels = c(AttritDurExp = "Attrition x Vote Method")),
  AffPol = clean_regress(da.s1, dvs = "AttritDurExp", type = "logistic", predictors = ~ messageType * AffPol_Pre, dv_labels = c(AttritDurExp = "Attrition x Baseline AffPol"))
)

# Display each interaction model table using cleanresults stargazer style
purrr::walk(res_da_int_list, ~ print(cr_table(.x, style = "stargazer")))

Differential Speeder Exclusion by Condition

The preregistration states: “If differential exclusion is observed (i.e., if the ‘speeders’ are disproportionately found in the treatment condition), we will perform sensitivity analyses to see how the results change if the speeders are included.” The 10-minute exclusion is not applied to the primary sample (the sensitivity models that apply it are in the “save models for supplement” chunk of 05_results_effects.Rmd). The tests below check whether speeders (completion time of 600 seconds or less) are distributed differently across conditions, mirroring the differential-attrition tests above.

da.s1 <- da.s1 %>%
  mutate(Speeder = if_else(`Duration (in seconds)` <= 600, 1, 0, missing = NA))
da.s2 <- da.s2 %>%
  mutate(Speeder = if_else(`Duration (in seconds)` <= 600, 1, 0, missing = NA))

table(da.s1$Speeder, da.s1$messageType)

##     Qualtrics  + Adversarial Dialogue Qualtrics + Belief-Tailored

##   1                                 9                           6

##   1  5.957447             6.435644                                 5.785124
# chi-square version  - nothing sig
report(chisq.test(da.s1$Speeder, da.s1$messageType))
## Effect sizes were labelled following Funder's (2019) recommendations.
## 
## The Pearson's Chi-squared test of independence between da.s1$Speeder and
## da.s1$messageType suggests that the effect is statistically not significant,
## and tiny (chi2 = 7.31, p = 0.198; Adjusted Cramer's v = 0.04, 95% CI [0.00,
## 1.00])
report(chisq.test(da.s1$Speeder, da.s1$ConditionChat))
## Effect sizes were labelled following Funder's (2019) recommendations.
## 
## The Pearson's Chi-squared test with Yates' continuity correction of
## independence between da.s1$Speeder and da.s1$ConditionChat suggests that the
## effect is statistically not significant, and tiny (chi2 = 0.27, p = 0.600;
## Adjusted Cramer's v = 0.00, 95% CI [0.00, 1.00])
report(chisq.test(da.s1$Speeder, da.s1$ConditionFeedback))
## Effect sizes were labelled following Funder's (2019) recommendations.
## 
## The Pearson's Chi-squared test of independence between da.s1$Speeder and
## da.s1$ConditionFeedback suggests that the effect is statistically not
## significant, and tiny (chi2 = 3.96, p = 0.138; Adjusted Cramer's v = 0.04, 95%
## CI [0.00, 1.00])
report(chisq.test(da.s2$Speeder, da.s2$ConditionFeedback))
## Effect sizes were labelled following Funder's (2019) recommendations.
## 
## The Pearson's Chi-squared test of independence between da.s2$Speeder and
## da.s2$ConditionFeedback suggests that the effect is statistically not
## significant, and tiny (chi2 = 0.09, p = 0.958; Adjusted Cramer's v = 0.00, 95%
## CI [0.00, 1.00])

Conversation Details

# quick distribution check
summary(df_convos$EvidenceFreq)
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.    NA's 
##   0.000   0.000   0.000   4.673   3.000 999.000       5
quantile(df_convos$EvidenceFreq, probs = c(.95, .975, .99), na.rm = TRUE)
##   95% 97.5%   99% 
## 12.00 18.65 65.24
# IQR rule
q1 <- quantile(df_convos$EvidenceFreq, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
q3 <- quantile(df_convos$EvidenceFreq, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
iqr <- q3 - q1
upper_iqr <- q3 + 1.5 * iqr

# cap based on ~600 words total 
cap <- 15

df_convos <- df_convos %>%
  mutate(
    EvidenceFreq_flag = EvidenceFreq > cap,
    EvidenceFreq_winsor = pmin(EvidenceFreq, cap)
  )


# winsorize
df_convos_winsor <- df_convos %>%
  mutate(EvidenceFreq = pmin(EvidenceFreq, cap))


#evidence frequency info

Post-Hoc Power Check

~80% power for Study 1 pairwise comparisons, ~52-56% for Study 2. target N reflected practical constraints and an expected d ~ 0.2 from Costello et al. (2024). This checks achieved power post hoc for each pairwise condition comparison, using pwr.t2n.test() since group sizes are unequal.

pacman::p_load(pwr)

# actual per-condition n's in the analytic sample (the 10-minute exclusion is not applied)
n_cond <- table(df_both$Study, as.character(df_both$ConditionFeedback))
power_pairs <- tribble(
  ~Study, ~Comparison,                                      ~n1,                                 ~n2,
  1,      "Adversarial vs. Belief-Tailored",                n_cond["1", "Adversarial Dialogue"], n_cond["1", "Belief-Tailored"],
  1,      "Adversarial vs. Belief & Values-Tailored",       n_cond["1", "Adversarial Dialogue"], n_cond["1", "Belief & Values-Tailored"],
  1,      "Belief-Tailored vs. Belief & Values-Tailored",   n_cond["1", "Belief-Tailored"],      n_cond["1", "Belief & Values-Tailored"],
  2,      "Control vs. Adversarial",                        n_cond["2", "Control"],              n_cond["2", "Adversarial Dialogue"],
  2,      "Control vs. Belief-Tailored",                    n_cond["2", "Control"],              n_cond["2", "Belief-Tailored"],
  2,      "Adversarial vs. Belief-Tailored",                n_cond["2", "Adversarial Dialogue"], n_cond["2", "Belief-Tailored"]
)

d_expected <- 0.2  # conservative from study 1

power_check <- power_pairs %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(power = pwr.t2n.test(n1 = n1, n2 = n2, d = d_expected,
                               sig.level = 0.05, alternative = "two.sided")$power) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(power_pct = paste0(round(power * 100, 1), "%"))

power_check %>%
  kable(caption = "Post-hoc power to detect d = 0.2 by pairwise condition comparison", align = "l") %>%
  kable_classic(full_width = FALSE, html_font = "Times New Roman") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "responsive"), font_size = 12)

# reverse: what n per arm (equal n) would be needed for 80% power at d = 0.2?
pwr.t.test(d = d_expected, sig.level = 0.05, power = 0.80, type = "two.sample", alternative = "two.sided") #1180 = 393 *3
## 
##      Two-sample t test power calculation 
## 
##               n = 393.4057
##               d = 0.2
##       sig.level = 0.05
##           power = 0.8
##     alternative = two.sided
## 
## NOTE: n is number in *each* group
#pre-post (paired) version ----
# type="paired" treats d as Cohen's d_z - the standardized mean of the PRE-POST DIFFERENCE scores (mean_diff / SD_diff), not the same quantity as the between-groups d = 0.2 used
pwr.t.test(d = d_expected, sig.level = 0.05, power = 0.80, type = "paired", alternative = "two.sided") #594 = 198*3
## 
##      Paired t test power calculation 
## 
##               n = 198.1508
##               d = 0.2
##       sig.level = 0.05
##           power = 0.8
##     alternative = two.sided
## 
## NOTE: n is number of *pairs*

Sensitivity Analysis

instead of assuming d = 0.2, checks what power we had

sensitivity_check <- power_pairs %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(min_detectable_d = pwr.t2n.test(n1 = n1, n2 = n2, power = 0.80,
                                          sig.level = 0.05, alternative = "two.sided")$d) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(min_detectable_d = round(min_detectable_d, 3))

sensitivity_check %>%
  kable(caption = "Minimum detectable effect size at 80% power", align = "l") %>%
  kable_classic(full_width = FALSE, html_font = "Times New Roman") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "responsive"), font_size = 12)
